name: make-website-agent-ready
description: Make a website ready for AI agents: runs the Hostinger agent readiness scan on the live site, ranks the failed checks by points lost, fixes them in the local codebase (robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt, head tags, JSON-LD, contact and pricing links, server-rendered content, Link headers, Markdown negotiation, WebMCP tools, MCP server card), verifies each fix against a local build, and reports what was fixed, skipped and left open. Never deploys. Triggers: make my site agent ready, agent readiness score, is my website AI-ready, improve my agent readiness grade, can ChatGPT / Claude read my site, add llms.txt, fix my agent readiness scan.

findings.excerpt: - Local: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' $B/robots.txt` prints 200, and the body is not blank.
- Local: `curl -s -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0)' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' $B/`. A block on the live site only is a CDN or WAF rule: off-site
- Local: `curl -s $B/sitemap.xml | head -c 400`. The sitemap's URLs must use the live `https://DOMAIN`, not localhost.
- Local: `curl -s $B/robots.txt | grep -i '^sitemap:'`. Use the absolute live URL.
- Local: `curl -s $B/sitemap.xml | grep -o '<lastmod>[^<]*' | sort | tail -1`. Emit lastmod from content dates or the build date.
- Local: `curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' $B/__agent-readiness-probe-0123456789ab`. SPA fallbacks that return 200 fail.
- Live only: `curl -sIL https://DOMAIN/ | grep -i '^location'`. HTTPS itself is hosting setup (`connect-domain` skill).
All read the raw homepage HTML: `curl -s $B/ > /tmp/home.html`.
- Local: `curl -sI -H 'Accept: text/markdown, text/plain;q=0.5' $B/ | grep -i '^content-type'`. Needs middleware or a server rule serving a Markdown version of
- Local: `curl -s $B/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json | python3 -m json.tool`. Only when the site runs an MCP server; the endpoint must be real.
